title: My hope is built on nothing less
composer: William B. Bradbury, 1863, Devotional Hymn and Tune Book, 1864
poet: Edward Mote, ca. 1834, Spiritual Magazine, alt.
lyrics:
My hope is built on nothing less than Jesus' blood and righteousness.
I dare not trust the sweetest frame, but wholly lean on Jesus' name.

  On Christ, the solid rock, I stand; all other ground is sinking sand,
  all other ground is sinking sand.

When darkness veils his loving face, I rest upon unchanging grace.
In ev'ry rough and stormy gale, my anchor holds within the vale.

  On Christ, the solid rock, I stand; all other ground is sinking sand,
  all other ground is sinking sand.

His oath, his covenant, and blood, support me in the 'whelming flood.
When all around my soul gives way, he then is all my hope and stay.

  On Christ, the solid rock, I stand; all other ground is sinking sand,
  all other ground is sinking sand.

Not earth, nor hell, my soul can move; I rest upon unchanging love.
I trust his righteous character, his counsel, promise, and his pow'r.

  On Christ, the solid rock, I stand; all other ground is sinking sand,
  all other ground is sinking sand.

When he shall come with trumpet sound, oh, may I then in him be found,
dressed in his righteousness alone, faultless to stand before the throne.

  On Christ, the solid rock, I stand; all other ground is sinking sand,
  all other ground is sinking sand.
